recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No follow-up core source change is recommended for FHIR-20676 unless Patient Care wants a new, explicit cross-resource reporting workflow model rather than the current IG-guided approach.
issue_request: FHIR-20676 was a Published FHIR-core Patient Care change request, resolved Persuasive with Modification for R5. It asked to revise AdverseEvent wording so the resource covers any change in patient status that may relate to unintended effects, including potential or avoided events, and to add that one adverse event may be reported in multiple ways with reporting form left to implementation guides.
initial_application: The Jira comment points to git commit 9e8268a, which applied GF#20676 by adding the single-event/multiple-reporting workflow-guidance sentence to source/adverseevent/adverseevent-introduction.xml and by updating the AdverseEvent root definition in the then-authoritative spreadsheet to the requested current-patient-status wording.
additional_context: AdverseEvent remains active in source/fhir.ini. Later Patient Care work reworked the same AdverseEvent narrative and root definition: FHIR-37780 moved the resource toward Clinical Care and Clinical Research IG usage, FHIR-38812 changed narrative terminology from research subject to research participant, FHIR-38905 added post-market reporting language to the root definition, and FHIR-39338 clarified neighboring boundaries. The current StructureDefinition carries the substantive FHIR-20676 definition with those later refinements, while the current introduction preserves the multiple-reporting/implementation-guide guidance.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Re-adding the 2019 wording verbatim would duplicate or partially roll back later Patient Care-approved wording; the current source already conveys the issue's implementer-facing rule through the active StructureDefinition and introduction text.
